suggestions.title: Ownership check compares head.repo.full_name with the stored project.githubRepo, so a renamed or transferred repo makes every PR look foreign
suggestions.failurePath: project.githubRepo = 'octo/demo' and the repo is later renamed on GitHub to 'octo/demo2' or moved to another org. projects.ts gives no way to update githubRepo (PATCH rejects the key), and GitHub redirects the old path, so the daemon's clone, its gh probe and the server's GET repos/octo/demo/pulls/N all keep working. The pulls response carries head.repo.full_name = 'octo/demo2'. At line 521 this does not equal target.fullName, so each review card gets the hint 'may be someone's fork PR' every round and is never finished or failed, even though the PR is the build's own. Nothing wrong is written, and the card stays in review as it does on main, but the reconcile never works for that project and the hint misleads. Comparing head.repo against base.repo from the same response (full_name or id) would still reject forks and would follow renames.

suggestions.title: A response with head.repo null (deleted fork) is re-read on every sweep without an ETag and never leaves a hint
suggestions.failurePath: The build's recorded PR is a fork PR (the probe matched on branch name only), and the fork was later deleted, so head.repo is null for good. Each sweep runs pullCache.delete(key) and counts the read as unreadable, so the next sweep sends a full GET with no If-None-Match. With a token that is about 60 full reads an hour per card for as long as it sits in review. Without a token it is 12 of the reconcile's 20 anonymous reads an hour per such card, and the card never gets a row explaining why. Test [62d] pins 'no hint'. A per-round hint, or caching the null-repo result as foreign, would bound this.

suggestions.title: Spec 02 and the ci-loop header say the reconcile and the grind together make at most 50 anonymous requests an hour; the grind is not capped
suggestions.failurePath: The text says '对账自己每小时至多 20 个匿名请求、连同磨绿至多 50 个', and the ci-loop.ts header has the same wording. In code, recordGrindAnonRead only counts the grind's reads and never blocks them; takeAnonRead stops only the reconcile once anonAll reaches 50. One anonymous card in building already makes about 60 check-runs reads an hour, so the combined total goes past 50 while the reconcile is starved. The PR body describes this correctly ('stops when it and the grind together reach 50'); the spec sentence reads as a cap on the total.

suggestions.title: The squash procedure in CLAUDE.md would land the stale round-1 commit message in main
suggestions.failurePath: CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md (Git section) says to take the squash subject and body from `gh api repos/xiechimon/pacman/pulls/1414/commits -q '.[0].commit.message'`. That returns 39990abc's message. It describes rules that later rounds replaced. Candidates were keyed on spec 23 latestPrBuild; the code now uses todo.latestBuildId. A closed PR went to failed on the first read; the code now confirms over two reads. It also has no ownership check, no once-per-round markers, and no anonymous budget. A merger who follows the documented procedure puts a commit into main whose message contradicts the code it contains. The PR body's Issues section asks for a hand-written squash message instead. The two instructions conflict, and only the PR body gets it right.
suggestions.evidence: PR body, Issues section: "the first commit's message (what `.[0].commit.message` returns) does not describe the code at the head. Squash with this message instead". Commit 39990abc body: "which are the todo's latest PR build (spec 23 latestPrBuild ...)" and "closed without merge: build.errorMessage names the PR, todo -> failed".

suggestions.title: Mechanism acceptance rests only on mocked GitHub response bodies, with no live capture of the fields used to decide
suggestions.failurePath: CLAUDE.md: "机制类改动，验收取实物 ... 判据字段 必须从 ... 该形态运行时真值上取实物；读源码、看配置 ... 都不算验收". The reconcile decides done or failed from GitHub fields: merged, head.ref, head.repo.full_name, base.ref, base.repo.default_branch, merged_by.login, and the compare status with per_page=1. The tests check these only against hand-written mock bodies. No live pulls/{n} or compare response is recorded in docs/verify/1403. The evidence files contain no full_name or default_branch capture. If a field name or shape differs in practice, the code treats the response as unreadable and the card stays in review. No test or evidence file would show the difference. The PR defers the live read to segment 3 and the host leg (待宿主).
suggestions.evidence: git grep for full_name|default_branch|merged_by in docs/verify/1403 finds only a test assertion message. PR body: "Host leg, not a task here ... segment 3 records a live read against the public repo".

suggestions.title: ⑭a's real scenario, a fix commit pushed after the merge (compare status 'behind'), has no test
suggestions.failurePath: The reconcile calls compare/{checkpoint}...{mergedHead}. When a fix round pushes a commit on top of the head that was merged, the checkpoint descends from the merged head, and GitHub answers status 'behind'. That is the case ⑭a describes ('the branch has a later commit the merge does not contain'), but ⑭a (pr-reconcile.test.ts:702) stubs 'diverged', and no test stubs 'behind'. I changed line 622 to `status !== 'ahead' && status !== 'identical' && status !== 'behind'`, which would finish a card whose last fix never reached the default branch. All 113 tests still pass. The code at head is correct; only the guard for the most likely input is unpinned.
suggestions.evidence: Mutation 'behind counted as contained' gives 'Tests 113 passed (113)'. The test file contains no `compare: 'behind'` anywhere.

suggestions.title: Split-wave advance on the reconcile's merged-to-done path (ticket scope) is not asserted anywhere
suggestions.failurePath: Ticket #1403's scope for a merged PR is 'done + system 行写合并 SHA + 推进 split 波次' (done, a system row with the merge SHA, and advancing the split waves). The ㉟ header comment in pr-reconcile.test.ts:63 claims '推进拆卡波次' (advances the split waves), but test ㉟ (line 1202) checks only phase and DONE_ROW. The single failure there is chief-tools.test.ts, which reads docs/research/assets/r5/raw/chief-threads-testA.json; my export did not include that file, and the same test fails the same way at head without the mutation. So nothing guards a split child whose PR is merged on GitHub against leaving its parent's next wave unscheduled.

suggestions.title: ⑱c pins the pending-decision path where a merge on GitHub is never reported (the ticket's core failure)
suggestions.failurePath: 1. A GitHub-form card is in review, and a person starts the merge. 2. The merge step merges main into the branch and pushes, but does not merge the PR (the ticket's 'Current state'). 3. finishTodoDone writes DONE_ROW and the card goes to done. 4. The person sees the PR still open, drags the card back to review, and merges the PR on GitHub. 5. On the next sweep, rowKnown(DONE_ROW, since) is true, so the reconcile counts settledBefore and returns (ci-loop.ts:532). The card stays in review with no merged row: the failure #1403 was opened for. ⑱c asserts exactly this, so segment 2 has to flip ⑱c. The PR discloses it in Risk, and the needs-decision label holds the merge, so this is not a new blocker.

DONE_ROW : closedText, since))`. ⑱c expects phase 'review' and no 'PR #n 已在 GitHub 合并' row after finishTodoDone, then a reopen, then a merged read. The member comment of 2026-10-21 confirms the label stays until a decision is made.

suggestions.title: [59] passes on origin/main for the wrong reason: a bare toThrow() is satisfied by finishTodoDone being undefined
suggestions.failurePath: `expect(() => finishTodoDone(...)).toThrow()` has no matcher. On origin/main the import is undefined, so the call throws a TypeError and the test passes; it was one of the 42 cases green on main in my run. At head the test is meaningful, because an early assert placed after stopUnclaimedGateSteps would leave the verify step stopped. Even so, any throw at all, including a TypeError, satisfies the assertion. Asserting `toThrow('illegal phase transition')` would make it fail for the right reason before the implementation exists.
suggestions.evidence: Head tests on origin/main sources: '✓ [59] the merge step finishing a card a person closed meanwhile throws before it stops anything'.

suggestions.title: GitHub-sourced branch names and merger login are embedded unbounded in conversation system rows that agents can read
suggestions.failurePath: Someone with write access to the target repo retargets the build's own PR to a branch whose name carries instruction-like text (git refs allow punctuation and CJK with no spaces) and merges it. The ownership check passes because the head is the conv branch, so reconcileOne writes the hint '...合并进了分支「<baseRef>」，不是默认分支「<defaultBranch>」...' verbatim into the build conversation. A chief or MCP agent that later calls the 'conversation' read tool sees that text as tool-result data. The same applies to pull.mergedBy at line 640, but GitHub logins are a restricted charset. The actor already needs write access to the repo, and the text reaches agents as data, not as a system layer. I traced no concrete wrong state transition. Bounding the length or allow-listing the characters of baseRef/defaultBranch before interpolation would close it cheaply.
suggestions.evidence: ci-loop.ts:543-549 interpolates pull.baseRef and pull.defaultBranch, and ci-loop.ts:638-645 interpolates pull.mergedBy. github.ts githubPull accepts any string for head/base ref fields. chief-tools.ts:427-435 and mcp-face.ts:215-223 return message.content to agents.
